title: Kalamatianos (chain dance)
summary: A Greek circle and chain dance in a seven-beat rhythm, led by the dancer at the front who waves a handkerchief while the line follows in joined hands.
howToPlay: Four places are lit beside the line: Step, Cross, Lift and the leader's Turn.
A ring closes on a place when that movement is due. Tap the place as the ring closes and the whole line answers.
The rhythm has seven beats to the bar: count it three, two, two.
rules: A tap right on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and taps with no ring open cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through; every pattern is counted in sevens.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the dance, not choreography to copy.
heritageNote: The Kalamatianos is danced across Greece at weddings and village celebrations. Dancers hold hands at shoulder height in an open circle or a line that curves around the square; the leader at the head of the line sets the steps and often holds a handkerchief, which is waved and turned as the line follows.
